label: There are epistemic reasons: some agent has an epistemic reason to believe some content
paraphrase: There are epistemic reasons: some agent has an epistemic reason to believe some content. Floor item F6 (#1007).

self_evident.note: Floor item F6 (#1007), approved by the owner on the common-ground basis; the approval plus that basis is the evidence (owner, 2026-11-05), so no stating text is pinned. Closest texts, cited but not yet pinned as claims: Terence Cuneo, The Normative Web (OUP 2007), on the parity of moral and epistemic normativity; Bart Streumer, Unbelievable Errors (OUP 2017), the full-strength rival. Justification: the owner's retorsion, certified as EPISTEMIC-NIHILISM-SELF-UNDERMINING (under nihilism no one has an epistemic reason to believe it). That shows nihilism self-undermining, not false: the same result certifies an interpretation in which nihilism holds and no one has a reason to believe it, which is Streumer's position. The rival stays recorded and unrefuted.
